In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and optimization of the parasitic bipolar structure, aiming to achieve the area-efficient and high-performance dual-diode with the lateral parasitic bipolar for the ESD protections in the I/O interfaces.

the design and optimization of the parasitic bipolar transistor inside the P+/N-wells diode, and a dual-diode with the optimized parasitic bipolar is proposed for the rail-based ESD protection in I/O interface ICs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lateral parasitic bipolar structure is very promising for the ESD protection in I/O interface ICs, and the optimized parasitic PNP structure can be used for the area-efficient dual diode with the ESD protection capability up to 8 kV HBM.
the parasitic PNP with optimized geometry parameters can be used as an alternative solution for the ESD protections with rail-based structures.
the lateral parasitic bipolar structure has the potential of providing a dual-diode with a low trigger voltage and high failure current for the I/O interface ESD protection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parasitic PNP is scalable and can be used to improve the area efficiency of ESD protections in ICs.

the breakdown behavior of lateral parasitic PPN is strongly influenced by geometry parameters, and the lateral parasitic bipolar structure can be optimized to achieve the area-efficient dual-diode ESD protections.
an area-efficient dual-diode (i.e., diodes in parallel) with optimized parasitic PNP structure can be achieved by using the finger-type parasitics.

the parasitic PNP with optimized geometry can be used as an effective ESD protection for high-voltage I/O interface applications.
